title: Case workspace frame (typed panels)
statement: UNB-UI-S-009 MUST be implemented as one frame with these regions in order: (1) Case header - work-item reference (G-016), subject reference and subject status lozenge, work-item status, owner, preparer, age against SLA, and the blocked outcome; (2) Rule that raised it - creating rule id and version, the condition that fired, and the exit condition that will close the item automatically; (3) Evidence region - typed evidence from the selected panel, each fact with source and freshness (G-003), conflicting sources side by side, and an evidence snapshot id; (4) Panel slot - exactly one typed decision panel (UNB-UI-P-*); (5) Decision record - proposed and recorded decisions with decider, authority, rationale, evidence snapshot and resulting subject transition, append-only; (6) AI summary flyout - opened by 'Explain', labelled 'AI-generated, not a decision' with sources, with no consequential controls (G-011); (7) Handoff - a handoff summary of what was done, what is pending and who acts next, plus reassignment. The panel MUST be selected deterministically from the work-item type, defined as (creating rule family, subject aggregate and workflow id, subject's current state), through a versioned panel registry; when the subject's state changes, the panel MUST re-resolve. If no panel is registered for a type, the slot MUST show 'No decision panel for this case type' and offer only Request evidence and Escalate; it MUST NOT fall back to a generic approve control. Every panel inherits from the frame: segregation of duties (decision controls disabled with a visible reason for the preparer, the proposer, the originator of the subject action and any user the subject transition's guards exclude, WFM-23-T11 decider-not-preparer); authority revalidation at submit, so a revocation within 60 seconds (RCD-041) rejects the decision; the G-005 confirmation naming the subject transition, its reversibility and who acts next; and G-006 unknown-outcome handling (no automatic retry). Recording a decision writes the WFM-23 decision record and issues the panel's subject transition; if execution fails the item shows 'Reopened' with the failure reason. Request evidence and Escalate are frame actions available in every panel; the frame MUST NOT offer bulk decisions across cases except the RCD-005 batch grant approval, which lives in the inbox (UNB-UI-S-008).
actions: Request evidence (A1; WFM-23-T04)
Escalate for authority (A1; WFM-23-T08)
Propose decision with evidence snapshot (A1; WFM-23-T09)
Record decision through the selected panel - decider holds authority and is not the preparer (A4; WFM-23-T11)
Reassign with reason (A2; WFM-23-T03)
Explain - open AI summary, read-only (A0; drafted by WFM-23-T10)
responsive: desktop-first (phone-review-and-approve for approve and decline only)

title: Charitable default disposition panel
statement: The panel MUST open on one of three subtypes named in its header (Succession, Dormancy, Closure residual) and MUST show: (1) the program terms version pinned on the case with the named charitable default recipients and their shares (source: program terms store; immutable on the case); (2) the trigger evidence for the subtype: Succession - the verified death notice and the successor-outreach log showing no eligible successor (WFM-20); Dormancy - the last qualifying activity date (activity projection, with freshness) against the inactivity window (default 36 months) and the outreach evidence per verified channel with delivery outcome (notification delivery records); Closure - the date the recommendation window elapsed; (3) the proposed distribution as a table of recipient, share and amount computed from available balance net of reservations, accrued fees and approved-unpaid grants (ledger, with as-of time); (4) each default recipient's current common charity status lozenge with its IRS-observation freshness (WFM-06). An ineligible or held recipient MUST be flagged with the text 'This charity will be held in the grant lifecycle; you will be asked to choose an alternative' because distributions run through the normal grant lifecycle. Decision options MUST be exactly: Approve charitable default (subtype transition), and for Dormancy only, Hold disposition and, from 'Disposition held', Resume outreach. The panel MUST NOT offer: editing recipients, shares or amounts (program terms change only through UNB-UI-S-010); any escheat or transfer of the fund balance to a state; direct payment (approval only creates grant recommendations); approval while the activity projection is not current (G-003) or the outreach evidence is incomplete, shown as blockers in the readiness checklist. If qualifying activity is detected at commit, the decision MUST NOT be recorded and the panel MUST show 'Active - activity detected since proposal'. The panel renders in the panel slot of the case workspace frame and inherits its segregation-of-duties, confirmation (G-005), unknown-outcome (G-006) and AI-labelling (G-011) rules.

Approve charitable default - dormancy; not the preparer; no escheat (A4; WFM-21-T08)
Hold disposition - dormancy (A4; WFM-21-T09)
Resume outreach (A2; WFM-21-T10)
Approve charitable default - closure residual; not the preparer (A4; WFM-22-T10)

title: Succession allocation panel
statement: The panel MUST show: the verified death or incapacity notice; each successor with identity verification and sanctions status and their freshness; open contests; the program rules version; and the allocation preview at the sponsor-designated valuation point (fund value, reservations, accrued fees, approved-unpaid grants, net allocable) with each successor's share and amount as a read-only allocation summary; for 'Split held', the constraint that failed (minimum, restriction, illiquidity, open commitment). Options MUST be: Split held - Decide split constraint (within program rules; recomputes the allocation); Allocation proposed - Activate succession. The panel MUST NOT offer: activation while a contest is open, a successor is unverified or not sanctions-clear, or the allocation is unbalanced; activation by break-glass access; editing shares outside program rules; allocation to another legal sponsor (that is an outbound transfer, WFM-22). If capacity changed since the preview, the decision is not recorded and the panel shows a new preview in 'Allocation proposed'. The panel renders in the panel slot of the case workspace frame and inherits its segregation-of-duties, confirmation (G-005), unknown-outcome (G-006) and AI-labelling (G-011) rules.

title: Unknown payment panel
statement: The panel MUST show: the payment chain (grant reference, amount, pinned destination version, provider idempotency key, dispatch time, dispatcher); the provider status-query history (each query time and response); the rail settlement window and when it elapsed; bank-statement reconciliation (statement date, debit found or not); recipient confirmation of non-receipt (source, channel, date); and the aging tier with days in 'Status unknown' against the final tier (default 30 days, RCD-042). The four NotReceived evidence items (settlement window elapsed, provider attests no execution, no statement debit, recipient confirms non-receipt) MUST be a readiness checklist with source and freshness each. Options MUST be: Check status (G-006, query by idempotency key); Declare not received - create replacement, enabled only when all four items are present and current and the decider is not the dispatcher; and, only after the final aging tier, Resolve by recorded decision requiring two independent treasury approvers, a duplicate-risk acceptance and a recovery plan (RCD-042). The panel MUST NOT offer: resend, retry or reissue of any kind outside these options; 'Mark paid' or 'Mark failed'; a single-approver override; both approvals by the same person; approval by the dispatcher. The panel renders in the panel slot of the case workspace frame and inherits its segregation-of-duties, confirmation (G-005), unknown-outcome (G-006) and AI-labelling (G-011) rules.

title: Sanctions post-block release panel
statement: The panel MUST resolve only when the subject's screening state is 'Blocked – OFAC report due' or 'Blocked – reported', or a dependent grant, ACH payment or check is 'Blocked'; for any other state, including 'Potential match – on hold' and 'Escalated to compliance officer', it MUST NOT be selectable and no release control exists. It MUST show: the confirmed match and its decision record (read-only); the blocked property items with ledger amounts and as-of time; the OFAC report due date (10 business days), filing status and annual-report tracking; licence evidence (OFAC licence number, issue and expiry dates, scope: named parties, property and transactions covered) with each blocked item marked 'Covered' or 'Not covered' by that scope; delisting evidence (list name, delisting publication date and list version, source); and for an ACH payment whether it was dispatched. Options MUST be: Release licensed property (subject stays a confirmed match; only covered items move); Record delisting (re-screen queued); Release blocked grant under licence or delisting; Release blocked ACH payment under licence (not yet dispatched only); Record blocked funds returned under licence; Release blocked check under licence (void confirmed). Every release re-enters all release gates. The panel MUST NOT offer: release of any item not covered by the licence scope; release with an expired licence; retry or reissue of a blocked payment; release by anyone other than an independent compliance officer at A4, or by the person who confirmed the match; any release control in the AI flyout. The panel renders in the panel slot of the case workspace frame and inherits its segregation-of-duties, confirmation (G-005), unknown-outcome (G-006) and AI-labelling (G-011) rules.

title: Charity hold panel - sponsor-only
statement: The panel MUST be visible only to the holding sponsor's compliance reviewers, within that sponsor's tenant context (G-010), and MUST show: the recipient's common status (read-only, as every sponsor sees it); the sponsor-only hold entry (HoldPublicationVersion, date, placer); the sponsor-private investigation notes and attachments, labelled 'Visible only to <sponsor>'; and whether a global hold also exists (status and reason class only). Options MUST be: Place sponsor-only hold (from 'Eligible'); Release sponsor-only hold (another compliance officer, not the placer); the record returns to 'Eligible' for this sponsor only. The panel MUST NOT offer: placing or releasing a global hold (escalation to platform compliance goes through the frame's Escalate, carrying reason class only); sharing or exporting notes to another sponsor; release by the placer; any hold or release control in the AI flyout. The panel renders in the panel slot of the case workspace frame and inherits its segregation-of-duties, confirmation (G-005), unknown-outcome (G-006) and AI-labelling (G-011) rules.
